newsitem.title: UK: Man cuts forecast for India 1997/98 sugar output.
newsitem.headline: Man cuts forecast for India 1997/98 sugar output.

text.p: Trade house E D & F Man cut its forecast of India's 1997/98 sugar production by 700,000 tonnes to 12.5 million tonnes white value, its latest monthly report showed on Tuesday.
The final result could be even less and with another lower crop anticipated, speculation was mounting as to when India might revert to net importer status, it said.
But with large stocks still to be run down, it was unlikely that such a change would occur before mid-1998.
"Estimates for the 1997/98 Indian crop have...been falling with the crop expected to show further falls from this year's lower estimated level," Man said.

Planting areas were expected to be lower in many cane-producing states, where replacement with other crops had taken place, and some southern states had already reduced areas after a spate of cyclones.
Man said its revised India estimate represented a fall of 24 percent, or almost four million tonnes, from last season.
It noted that the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) had also cut its production estimate to 13 million tonnes white value whilst the Ministry of Food was maintaining a forecast of 14 million.
